macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks approach record highs as yields and oil prices ease
items.summary: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq reached record highs as Treasury yields retreated from multi-year peaks and oil prices declined. Investors are also positioning ahead of the quarterly earnings season.

items.title: Fed plans overhaul of bank-supervision structure
items.summary: Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman said the central bank plans to replace its current regional supervisory model with five geographic regions led by regional leaders, increasing accountability to Washington.

items.title: Markets reduce expectations for near-term Fed rate hike
items.summary: A weaker-than-expected payrolls report has lowered expectations for an imminent rate increase, with traders pricing a 78% probability that the Fed will leave rates unchanged this month. The 30-year Treasury yield fell to 5.62% after reaching a 24-year high of 5.702%.

items.title: Asian stocks rise after Nasdaq record
items.summary: Asian equities advanced after the Nasdaq closed at a record, with MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan up 0.2% and Japan’s Nikkei up 0.7%; European equity futures also gained.

items.title: Software stocks hit 2026 highs on stronger earnings outlook
items.summary: The S&P 500 software and services index rose 1.3% to its highest level since November 2025. Gains followed solid results from companies including Salesforce, ServiceNow and Accenture and renewed enthusiasm for AI-related partnerships.

items.title: Constellation Energy jumps on Google power agreement
items.summary: Constellation Energy shares surged more than 12% after the company announced a 20-year power-purchase agreement with Google, making it one of the S&P 500’s strongest performers.

items.title: Tesla shares gain after strong third-quarter deliveries
items.summary: Tesla shares climbed more than 5% after the company reported third-quarter deliveries above 486,000 vehicles, exceeding production by approximately 22,000 units.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: CFTC proposes federal framework for crypto exchanges
items.summary: The CFTC unveiled a preliminary plan for regulating crypto exchanges, including federal licensing based on leverage, customer-asset segregation, reserve requirements and actual-delivery rules. The proposal is expected to enter a public-comment period.

items.title: FinCEN withdraws proposed crypto wallet and mixer rules
items.summary: FinCEN withdrew proposals that would have expanded reporting requirements for transactions involving unhosted wallets and crypto mixers, citing public feedback and a broader shift toward lighter digital-asset oversight.

items.title: Bitcoin remains near $86,000 as major tokens trade mostly flat
items.summary: Bitcoin was reported around $85,600-$86,300, down roughly 0.2%-0.9% over 24 hours. Ethereum traded near $2,715, while Solana was around $120; Zcash was a notable outperformer, rising about 4%.

items.title: SEC clears leveraged crypto and commodity exchange-traded funds
items.summary: The SEC cleared six funds offering triple-daily exposure to Bitcoin, Ethereum, gold, silver, oil and gas after a Cboe rule change, expanding access to highly leveraged products.

items.title: Polymarket announces Protocol V2
items.summary: Polymarket unveiled a protocol upgrade featuring unified contracts, pUSD collateral, cross-chain support and additional market types. Mainnet testing is scheduled through October 30.

items.title: Rain seeks U.S. trust-bank charter
items.summary: Stablecoin platform Rain applied to establish Rain National Trust Bank, which would provide institutional digital-asset custody, stablecoin-reserve and issuance services under OCC supervision.

items.title: Hyperliquid unlocks $340 million in HYPE tokens
items.summary: Hyperliquid released approximately 3.75 million HYPE tokens, valued at about $340 million, with the allocation reportedly going to a single institutional buyer.

items.title: OKB and Numeraire post sharp gains
items.summary: OKB briefly rose about 10% in 24 hours to above $140, while Numeraire reportedly surged roughly 42% in 15 minutes and nearly 50% over a short period to around $17.60.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Reflection unveils Beam open-weight AI model
items.summary: Reflection introduced Beam, a 501-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 23 billion active parameters, targeting coding, reasoning, and agent tasks. The company says it delivers competitive reasoning performance with substantially lower compute requirements than comparable models.[1][3]

items.title: Reka releases Rho-1 multimodal reasoning model
items.summary: Reka released Rho-1, a 19-billion-parameter research model designed to understand and generate text, images, and video while also producing robot actions. The model is currently a research preview without publicly available weights.[2]

items.title: Anthropic expands Claude Startups program
items.summary: Anthropic announced an expansion of its Claude Startups program, deepening the company’s engagement with founders and rapidly growing AI companies.[6]

items.title: OpenAI plans EU text watermarking for ChatGPT and Codex
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly plans to add text watermarking for ChatGPT and Codex users in the European Union to support compliance with the EU AI Act, with an opt-in option for API customers worldwide.[8]

items.title: NASA and IBM release lunar science foundation model
items.summary: NASA, IBM Research, and academic partners released an open-source foundation model focused on lunar science, positioning it among the earliest models tailored to scientific analysis of the Moon.[7]

items.title: South Korea plans multitrillion-won frontier AI program
items.summary: South Korea is planning a 4.7 trillion-won initiative to develop frontier AI models beginning in March 2027, signaling continued government investment in national AI capabilities.[2]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: AI-driven game mashups and PS5 emulation spark industry concerns
items.summary: New AI capabilities are enabling rapid creation of playable game mashups, while advances in PS5 emulation and a reported console exploit are raising concerns about intellectual property, platform security, and the future of game development.

items.title: Supermassive Games reportedly hit by major layoffs
items.summary: More than 70 developers reportedly appear to have left Supermassive Games this week, indicating another significant contraction at a prominent game studio.

items.title: Escape from Tarkov rolls out beginner-friendly PvE update
items.summary: Escape from Tarkov introduced a PvE update designed to make the game more accessible to new players, easing some of its notoriously demanding early-game experience.

items.title: Suri: The Seventh Note announced for October 30 on PS5
items.summary: PlayStation confirmed that Suri: The Seventh Note will launch on PS5 on October 30.

items.title: Esports remains part of Asian Games plans after rumors
items.summary: The Olympic Council of Asia reportedly denied claims that esports would leave the Asian Games after 2026, while announcing a separate Asian Esports and Mind Sports Games in Kuwait.
